hypothesis: Session load and attach-snapshot phases allocate several transient copies of the session body (whole-file String reads, parsed entry trees held alongside raw rows, deep-copied attach message trees); glibc keeps those freed pages resident per-arena for the process lifetime, so a grown session's load peak stays in RSS forever. Returning freed heap to the OS after each large transient phase + capping per-thread arenas should cut settled RSS of a loaded large session materially with no latency cost.
approach: New pa-types memory_release module: cap_thread_arenas() (mallopt M_ARENA_MAX 8) at startup in pa-cli and pa-daemon mains; trim_freed_heap() (malloc_trim(0)) after window walk/replay in agent_engine, after resumed create, after the hydrated-file command, after the TUI attach fold (all cfg-gated linux/gnu - macOS arm64 + non-glibc are no-ops); streamed line-by-line SessionFile::open (BufReader, no whole-body String; differential oracle tests vs the pre-streaming reference reader); windowed store raw/metadata rows consumed in place (take_raw_entries/take_metadata_entries, retained_ids from store ids, no third parse pass); TUI attach fold consumes the wire frame by move (attach_data_from_response takes Value). Final diff vs base f37144ff: 14 files +406/-28. Fold history: the #2824 split fold silently dropped two lane hunks (unstaged edits after --theirs) — caught via reviewer diff-count condition; d626a1a08 restored them; the #2871 split 5/5 fold re-homed the attach single-tree into worker/connection.rs where it now lives beside the post-frame-send trim_freed_heap_if_large call. All final-head measurements (gates + spot-check) ran on the committed tree as-is.
parity_notes: All changes are allocator plumbing and ownership moves; no data, capability, protocol, wire, prompt, or user-visible behavior changes. Non-glibc/non-Linux builds compile the helpers as no-ops (shipped platforms: Linux x86_64 glibc2.35+, Linux aarch64, macOS arm64). /effort GetConnectionState wire hunk NOT present in final diff; zero hunks touching GetConnectionState/GetState/worker_overloaded (typed-refusal backpressure surface untouched).
